Each round in Rolled West you will extract goods from the land based on a roll of the custom dice. Spend wood to make settlements and secure majorities in different terrain types. Use metals to fulfill contracts, make sales, or invest in a burgeoning boomtown. Bank resources during your opponents' turns to use later, and mark your choices on the included dry erase scoreboards. Will you come out on top at the end of 6 rounds? Number of players: 2 - 4 Game duration: 10 mn Complexity: 1 / 5 Play Rolled West and 1414 other games online. Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Resources are first spent from the rolled resources then the banked resources. The dice are 12 sided with 4 copper, 3 wood, 3 silver, and 2 gold. AREAS: Boomtown - (Top Left) - 3x3 grid of special bonus. Use only once per turn. Shipping - (Top Right) - Bonus for the 3rd and final 5th spot. The higher (top) bonus is available only to the player that first reaches this place. The lower bonus goes to all other players reaching this point. Contracts - (Middle Row) - Spend various copper, silver, gold. 5 Gold for 15 points being the highest. All contracts are unique so only can be claimed by 1 player in the whole game. Claims - (Bottom) - Spend 1-2 wood to make camp/settlement. After you choose the terrain. 1 wood (camp), 2 wood (settlement). The far right of this track show bonus for coming 1st (top) and 2nd (bottom). Numbers on the track denote an immediate score. TURN: Roll 4 dice. Choose Terrain: Select 1 dice as the terrain for a possible advancement on the 'Claims' track using additional wood. 1 Extra wood (camp), 2 Extra wood (settlement). Main Phase where you can use your dice and any previously banked resources. -- You may bank at most 1 dice in this phase to add to your banked resources. OPPONENTS TURN: - You get to bank 1 of the dice to add to your banked resources. Either copy a dice from the player to your left, or from your right, but just 1 dice total per round. There is an automated UI feature for this, if you prefer to automatically make this decision. [Rating: 1/10] Tossed after playing once. Barely a game. You roll the dice and do what you can with the results. Just bad, and the components are weak as well.

[Rating: 1/10] Theme does not appeal to me. Many options but does not feel satisfying as a roll and write.

[Rating: 2/10] Rolled West epitomizes the many shortcomings of roll-and-write games, while also shedding everything that makes the genre enjoyable. Aside from being able to save a resource during your off-turns, the game boils down to checking the highest scoring box each turn as the scoring system is overly straightforward and contains no subtleties. Gameplay is similarly lacking, and is void of both the fun combo-chaining and interesting press-your-luck elements typical of the genre. I often find roll-and-write criticism levied unfairly (ie. dice are random), but Rolled West is like the straw man argument 

[Rating: 2/10] Mimics the board game very well, but that is all about it. It's very lucky, besides the dice you reserve, you have no control about anything. I don't understand what's the selling point of this game with the current great proliferation of games of similar mechanics, and the parent board game is not one of the greats either.

[Rating: 3/10] There are so many roll & write games that Rolled West just doesn't stand a chance. It has very little for the players to do while waiting for their turn to roll - always a no-no in this genre for me.

[Rating: 3/10] I love Gold West and really enjoy Roll and write games. I figured this was a no brainer. Unfortunately, I did not like it. I tried a couple of times but will NEVER play it again. Luckily the game was not too expensive and I will keep the dice and promo for Gold West.

[Rating: 3/10] In a very crowded field of roll and write games, this one really doesn't offer anything new, and just plain felt unexciting to play.  Everything here reuses tired old mechanisms without putting them together in an interesting way.  I'm also not a fan of this style of roll and write where it's just checking off some boxes according to what you roll. I prefer ones like On Tour, where I have to make difficult decisions with the rolls, and there's more "game" and tension.

[Rating: 3/10] Just too many other roll and writes that I find much more enjoyable.  Didn't feel like this did anything special.

[Rating: 3/10] Even for a roll and write, this feels a little bit on the basic and uneventful end. It plays fine and flows fine, but ultimately, it's forgettable in an incredibly crowded space.

[Rating: 3/10] Roll and write that gets right to the point. Not really my genre given the low interaction but Rolled West was better than many and quick. + Liked the interactive parts of the scoring board

[Rating: 3/10] The scoring system for Gold West is probably the weakest part of the entire game because it is effectively "tracks", and Rolled West is pretty much just that scoring system.

[Rating: 4/10] It's okay, but it just doesn't feel thematic or exciting enough for me. It feels like you can get stuck doing one thing because there's no way to mitigate rolls, and it can be disappointing.

[Rating: 4/10] Not my cup of tea. Doesn't bring anything new to the so seen 'roll & write' -genre. Icons could be way more clearer too.

[Rating: 4/10] It's roll-and-write so it's starting from a low base, and magnifies its crime by being dull. Effectively you only get three dice to tick off stuff, so you don't get a lot of choice. The only passive action is to write down a resource either of your neighbours used to boost what you can do on your turn. Each resource has two races to compete in, so either use the resources you rolled to tick off and progress in these races, or complete a one-off project for a combo.
